newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU fails to agree on in vitro medical devices.
newsitem.headline: EU fails to agree on in vitro medical devices.

text.p: European Union ministers failed on Wednesday to reach full agreement on internal market rules for in vitro diagnostic medical devices.
France, Italy and other member states had difficulties with an element of the proposal concerning medical devices which include human tissues.

This aspect of the proposal will be sent back to EU ambassadors in a new bid to solve the issue by September. The original proposal sought to establish mutual recognition among member states concerning medical devices as a way to create a single market for such products in the EU.

"That is the most controversial issue," said one EU diplomat. He said France and Italy did not think the proposal included the necessary safeguards and that the best would be to take out the part concerning medical devices with human tissues altogether.
However, the ministers reached political agreement on three other difficult issues, including for example market surveillance provisions.

In vitro diagnostic devices are used outside the human body for medical examinations of samples taken from the patient. They are important tools for diagnosing illnesses, monitoring patients' state of health, as well as for AIDS, hepatitis and glucose tests, and pregnancy tests.
The proposal lays down the essential requirements which such devices must meet in order to be placed on the market and the conformity assessment procedures with which manufacturers must comply.
It sought to achieve a delicate balance between EU single market objectives of the free circulation of goods and of health protection.

Any malfunctioning of medical devices could lead to misdiagnosis with serious consequences, and Paris fears that the proposal would lower the country's standards in this field. "The French have strong doubts in general" about the proposal, the diplomat said.
